ETCSL 5.6.1 — The instructions of Šuruppag

  • Editors: ETCSL project (J. Black, G. Cunningham, E. Robson, G. Zólyomi et al.), Oxford 1998–2006
  • URLs: transliteration https://etcsl.orinst.ox.ac.uk/cgi-bin/etcsl.cgi?text=c.5.6.1&display=Crit&charenc=gcirc ; translation https://etcsl.orinst.ox.ac.uk/cgi-bin/etcsl.cgi?text=t.5.6.1 ; XML from OTA 2518 (see ../_bulk/). ORACC: https://oracc.museum.upenn.edu/epsd2/literary/Q000782
  • Retrieved: 2026-10-16 (live site down; HTML from Wayback Machine raw captures; XML from Oxford Text Archive)

Why it matters here

Šuruppag, son of Ubara-Tutu, gives counsel to his son Ziusudra (l. 1–13, repeated at 73–82 and 143–152). Gilgameš XI 23 calls Uta-napišti 'man of Šuruppak, son of Ubara-Tutu' — the Akkadian tradition knows this lineage; an Akkadian version of the Instructions exists (Lambert BWL; Alster 2005). Earliest versions: Fara and Abu Ṣalābīḫ (ED IIIa, c. 2600 BC). Standard edition: Alster, Wisdom of Ancient Sumer (2005).
